jobDescription: Brightmesh makes project-management software and answers roughly 9,000 support tickets a month across three regional queues. The Support Operations Analyst looks after the helpdesk configuration and macro library, produces the weekly backlog report for the support leads, tests configuration changes with agents before release and trains each intake of new agents on the tooling. The analyst is expected to have put routing or automation changes into live operation on a customer-facing queue and to watch their effect after release, working with the support leads and the IT change board. The analyst sits in customer-success operations and reports to the head of support.
requirements: Produces a weekly backlog and service-level report for the support leads.
Builds and maintains the macro library in the helpdesk platform.
Has put a ticket-routing or automation change into live operation on a customer-facing support queue and monitored it after release.
Runs user acceptance testing with support agents before configuration changes.
Trains new agents on the helpdesk tooling.

evidence.text: Support Operations Coordinator, Fenwick Software, January 2023 to September 2024. Compiled the weekly backlog report for four support leads, showing open tickets by age band and first-response times against the published targets.

Rewrote and maintained about 120 macros in the helpdesk platform, retiring duplicates and adding placeholders for the customer's plan and region; usage of each macro was reviewed every quarter from the helpdesk's macro report.
Designed language- and plan-based routing rules in the helpdesk's sandbox instance and replayed three months of historical tickets through them to compare queue assignments with the existing rules.
Organised two rounds of user acceptance testing with eight support agents in the sandbox, logging each defect in the IT tracker and retesting the fixes before sign-off.
Delivered a half-day tooling induction to every intake of new agents in 2024 (five intakes), covering views, macros and escalation paths.

Work sample: the UAT sign-off pack for the routing rules, holding the test scripts, the defect log and the agents' sign-off sheets, all run in the sandbox instance. Its last page, 'Go-live readiness', has every checklist line ticked and ends: 'Target: live on the EMEA queue from 2 September, pending change-board approval.'
Reference check summary: Fenwick Software's support director confirmed in writing that the candidate produced the weekly backlog report and ran the new-agent inductions during 2024.
HR verification note: the job title Support Operations Coordinator and the dates January 2023 to September 2024 were checked against the contract and payslips the candidate supplied, and they match.

propositions.text: The candidate compiled a weekly backlog report for four support leads showing open tickets by age band and first-response times.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the report and the reference check confirms it in writing.

propositions.text: The candidate put the new routing rules into live operation on the EMEA support queue from 2 September and monitored them after release.
propositions.rationale: The pack documents sandbox UAT, and its go-live line is a target date pending change-board approval; no source says the rules ran on a live queue. The deployment rule requires the environment and status to be kept as the source gives them, so a planned go-live in a sandbox pack is not live operation.

propositions.text: The candidate designed routing rules in the helpdesk's sandbox instance and ran two rounds of user acceptance testing with eight agents.
propositions.rationale: Both resume entries place the routing design and the testing in the sandbox instance.

gold.expectedGap: The routing rules are documented only in the sandbox instance and UAT; whether they were approved and switched on for a live queue is not documented.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Report the routing design, the historical replay and the UAT as sandbox work; keep the go-live line as a target pending change-board approval.
followUpTargets: Ask whether the change board approved the routing rules, who enabled them on a live queue and when, and what the candidate monitored after they were switched on.
